questions.question: What are all the conditions under which the landlord can enter the premises?
questions.expected: Reasonable prior notice (typically 24 hours) for inspection, maintenance or repair between 9AM and 8PM; no notice in a bona fide emergency; during the last 60 days to show the premises.
questions.answer:
Based on the provided context, the conditions under which the landlord can enter the premises are:

1. For the purpose of inspection, maintenance, or repair, upon providing reasonable prior notice (typically 24 hours) to the Tenant (Source 1, Section 16).
2. In the case of a bona fide emergency (e.g., fire, flood, or gas leak), the Landlord may enter the Premises without prior notice (Source 1, Section 16).
3. To address matters relating to the condition of the property, upon providing reasonable prior notice to the Tenant, except in the case of a bona fide emergency (Source 2, Section 5).
4. To conduct a move-in inspection and document the condition of the Premises via photos and/or video, which shall serve as a reference for the condition of the unit at the end of the tenancy (Source 3, Section 8).

Note that the context does not provide explicit conditions for entry in other situations, such as during a large gathering or party that disturbs the peace (Source 2, Section 5).
